reason: No paper, dataset or product flags crop pixels whose label stays constant but whose embedding is drifting, aimed at map maintainers. Closest is an arXiv anomaly detector that scores crop-labeled points against same-class neighbours to clean training data at one point in time, not to monitor a published annual map across years. A personal blog post shows the drift signal itself exists in AlphaEarth embeddings but builds no tool, is not crop-specific, and is unreviewed. CLMS documentation confirms the confidence layer measures per-date input uncertainty, not cross-year semantic instability.
